tables.title: Indexed dissertations and degree awards: pooled counts at matched institutions
tables.notes:
Table note: These bases overlap and are not successive exclusions. Population content profiles use their stated completed, applicable observations; uncertainty, structural inapplicability and incomplete processing remain separate. RQ1 measurement additionally distinguishes conditional agreement on jointly coded values from end-to-end correctness on reference-coded values, counting model nondelivery as nonmatches in the latter (S1).

We compared all-topic ProQuest dissertations and theses with degrees awarded to assess whether indexed research tracks university output over time. This helps interpret drug- and alcohol-related research counts, which may also change as ProQuest’s representation of university output changes. The comparison is independent of topical eligibility coding.

Indexed dissertations per 100 degree awards = 100 × summed indexed dissertations and theses ÷ summed degree awards at matched institutions. We compared master’s theses with all master’s awards and flagged research-doctorate dissertations with research/scholarship doctoral awards. These ratios describe indexed research relative to awards; they are neither degree-type shares nor direct database-capture estimates.

From 2010 to 2023, indexed research-doctorate dissertations increased by 8% while corresponding awards increased by 43%, reducing the ratio from 79.3 to 59.9 per 100 awards (Extended Table DEP1-E05). Master’s indexed theses and awards increased by 41% and 42%; their ratio was 3.1 at both endpoints, after rising to 4.2 in 2014 and then declining (DEP1 Figure F2).

The annual doctoral comparison expanded from 464 to 663 institutions. Among the same 411 institutions in all 14 years, indexed dissertations increased by 6% and awards by 32%, reducing the ratio from 80.8 to 65.2. Changing membership therefore cannot fully explain the decline. The prespecified RQ3 doctoral sensitivity uses this fixed institution group (S3). This fixed group is disproportionately NIH-supported: about 86% of its awards were at institutions supported in at least one relevant funding window, versus 53% outside the group (S3).

We matched dissertations to IPEDS institutions by year and counted each institution identifier once per award total. We required an approved match and available positive awards, retaining awards even when no dissertation was indexed. Extended Table DEP1-E04 reports pooled counts and matched institutions’ share of national awards; this share describes the award denominator, not dissertation capture. The supporting indexing tables give exclusions and ratios above 100, including the unresolved school/campus correspondence that required excluding the Chicago School.

tables.title: Indexed dissertations and degree awards in 2010 and 2023
tables.notes:
Table notes: We summed dissertations and awards before calculating ratios. National totals were 11,376,644 master’s and 981,947 research/scholarship doctoral awards. The stable group required positive doctoral awards and unchanged constituent IPEDS identifiers in all 14 years, without selecting on indexing ratios; it contributes 89.5% of matched doctoral awards. Panel B uses flagged research doctorates and whole-number percentage changes. Panel A’s upper doctoral counts add 4,302 unresolved classifications in matched comparisons; the endpoints reflect classification uncertainty, not confidence intervals or excluded degree cases.

Sources: ProQuest all-topic exports and 2010–2023 IPEDS Completions files downloaded 27 September 2026. We used cYYYY_a.csv, not _rv members, with first-major, all-fields totals (MAJORNUM=1, CIPCODE=99, CTOTALT) and award levels 7 (master’s) and 17 (research/scholarship doctoral). We matched July–June IPEDS reporting year to completion year without a shift, an approximate alignment.

Master’s awards include degrees without a thesis, and deposit/indexing practices may vary; indexed theses therefore do not represent all master’s graduates or support employment generalization to that population. ProQuest and IPEDS doctoral classifications, timing and institutional boundaries also differ, but we have not quantified their contributions to the discrepancies. Ratios above 100 account for 22.9% of matched flagged doctoral dissertations and reinforce why these are not capture percentages; some extreme comparisons remain unexplained. The declining doctoral ratio does not imply replacement by another doctorate type. We withheld a broader doctoral comparison because missing award rows could not reliably be distinguished from genuine zeros. These all-topic results raise a concern about representation over time but do not establish the size or direction of bias in drug- and alcohol-related research; we use neither adjustment factors nor funding covariates derived from these ratios.

tables.title: Award/person relationship accounting, primary plus-three window
tables.notes:
Search capture measures whether an identified award-associated work entered the candidate frame before abstract-assessability or inclusion-coding decisions. Final-inclusion coverage measures whether it subsequently entered the study population. All 820 primary matched works are indexed in the all-topic ProQuest frame. The primary base contains 786 doctoral and 34 master's works; 582 and 19, respectively, entered the population. Matching a work to an award holder does not establish that the award funded that particular degree. Works are counted once across repeated awards and mechanisms; the F30/F31 and R36 work bases overlap by two works. The clear-plus-possible base contains 829 doctoral and 39 master's works, of which 615 and 22 are included.

The topical search retrieved 598/775 F30/F31-associated works (77.2%) and 39/47 R36-associated works (83.0%) into the candidate frame. Final-inclusion coverage was 567/775 (73.2%; Wilson 95% CI 69.9–76.2%) for F30/F31 fellowships and 34/47 (72.3%; 58.2–83.1%) for R36 grants. The pooled union is a secondary accounting summary: 636/820 works were retrieved (77.6%) and 601/820 entered the population (73.3%).

tables.title: Timing and match-definition sensitivity, all mechanisms
tables.notes:
Scientific-undetermined and incomplete-processing counts are zero in these matched-work bases; both remain separate dispositions in the supporting tables. In the primary clear base, 184 works were not retrieved (22.4% of 820), 32 were retrieved but excluded (3.9%) and three lacked usable abstracts (0.4%). Of the 636 retrieved works, 633 had assessable abstracts and 601 entered the population. The four disposition columns in Table S1.10 are mutually exclusive; the 32 exclusions are adopted inclusion decisions rather than independently established coding errors.

Nonretrieval accounts for 184 of the 219 pooled works not included (84.0% of nonentry), so the observed gap arises mainly at retrieval rather than classification after retrieval. Here, not retrieved means that a work present in the all-topic ProQuest frame was absent from the topical query results; it does not mean that the work was absent from ProQuest. This is a stage-of-nonentry description; the substantive scope of nonretrieved works is unknown.

Non-retrieved works have title-only evidence here, so their substantive scope is unknown. An award is not proof that a dissertation meets this study's inclusion criteria. These estimates describe inclusion among identified, source-linked ProQuest works and remain conditional on identity-link validity while independent human validation is pending. They do not estimate coverage of all award recipients, degree completion, ProQuest indexing completeness or national search recall.

tables.title: Sensitivity models: 2021-2023 post period
tables.notes:
Baseline is 2014–2017. The NIDA×post coefficient times 100 is the adjusted difference in opioid-share changes, in percentage points. Positive estimates indicate an additional absolute increase among NIDA-connected works.

Controls are credential family, broad field, institution and completion year. Institution-cluster CR1 covariance uses actual full design rank and t reference with G−1 degrees of freedom. Pointwise intervals and two-sided raw p values accompany Holm adjustment across exactly these two primary completion-window tests.

Both pointwise intervals include zero and meaningful positive differences. These exploratory tests do not establish greater growth, equivalence, absence of an additional increase, or a causal funding effect. The two-test correction does not cover all exploratory decisions.

All models use the fixed 2014–2017 baseline. These are labeled sensitivity results, not additional primary tests; their raw p values have no primary two-test Holm adjustment.

All use the stated institution-cluster CR1/t inference. Alternate-comparator models include NIAAA-only works among all non-NIDA works; preceding-PI-only models exclude award-only positive connections while retaining the no-identified-NIDA/NIAAA comparator.

The four-cell restriction and institution-specific post shifts change the comparison structure. Their negative estimates do not establish a negative funding effect.

tables.title: Largest-institution deletion refits: descriptive ranges
tables.notes:
The linear estimate is percentage points per year; the block estimate is percentage points. The annual joint test has no single percentage-point estimate or interval. All models use the same eligible 2010–2017 primary pair, credential-family, field, institution and completion-year controls, and institution-cluster CR1 inference.

The annual joint test rejects constant adjusted annual NIDA–comparison gaps. Nonsignificant linear and block summaries do not establish parallel pretrends. These exploratory diagnostics weaken attribution to a 2018 policy change.

pretrend_annual_terms.csv supplies all seven annual interaction contrasts using 2017 as reference, with pointwise intervals and p values. No Holm adjustment is applied to this separate diagnostic set.

Within each primary sample, the five largest institutions by work count were deleted one at a time. The baseline remains 2014–2017 and each window retains its stated post period; the five institutions are not deleted jointly.

These ranges summarize ten existing refits; they are not confidence intervals. Exact individual estimates, intervals, p values, retained institution counts and original deleted sizes remain in `DEP3_opioid_largest_institution_deletions`, with institution identifiers omitted from this aggregate projection.

tables.title: Institutional support and dependence diagnostics
tables.notes:
Size-effective counts are squared total size divided by the sum of squared cluster sizes. Identifying-mass-effective counts use squared residualized interaction values after nuisance and NIDA-main-effect projection. These summarize concentration; they do not certify a number of independent information units.

Institution-cluster inference assumes sufficient independence across institutions. The broader historical institution-plus-PI graph has a component containing approximately 54.5% of each sample and a size-effective count near 3.3. Its covariance calculations are a limited sensitivity, not an uncertainty certification or replacement primary inference.

The broader-component 2022–2023-window lower confidence limit is −0.0011 pp at the displayed precision; it includes zero. Its raw p=.050056 is not reported as .05 or as significance. Coding, linkage, retrieval and source-selection uncertainty remain outside these intervals.

figures.title: Complete group profiles

Available 95% pointwise intervals, contributing-institution counts and source identifiers are supplied in DEP2 Tables T3. All PsyD and DrPH profiles meeting support are included.

figures.title: Complete institution profiles

figures.title: Complete content plates
captions: DEP3 Figure F2. Complete observed research-content profiles and connected-minus-remaining differences by degree under the identified NIDA/NIAAA funding-connection definition. Eight pages show all 44 categories across C3 study design, C4 level of analysis, C5 research objective and C8 data type, separately for research-doctorate dissertations and master's theses. Blue denotes works with a clear preceding-funded advisor/committee association or clear individual-award association, or both; orange denotes remaining works. A work is counted once. Filled circles show the full observed outcome-eligible groups. Open circles show the observed groups excluding whole institutions ever identified as for-profit; unknown ownership is retained. Group profiles are observed percentages; connected-minus-remaining contrasts are percentage points. Each page prints both group denominators for each ownership population. Profile scales are 0-100%; all contrast scales are -40 to +40 percentage points. Points are corpus descriptions; no intervals, covariate adjustment, prediction or overlap restriction are used. C3/C4/C5 categories are mutually exclusive within their coded outcome. C8 forms overlap and their shares can total above 100%. Missing, inapplicable and undetermined outcomes are excluded rather than zero-filled. The PI timing windows are five preceding fiscal years for research doctorates and two for master's, excluding completion FY; individual-award eligibility runs from the first observed funding FY through the last observed funding FY plus three, clipped to 2010-2023. No identified connection is not verified absence of support. The source-exact companion preserves all 616 observed targets, including 88 master's-minus-doctorate differences of the connected-minus-remaining contrasts. Those direct comparisons use four separate group denominators. Historical adjusted results are not included in this display.
Panel key: F2a/F2b study design; F2c/F2d level of analysis; F2e/F2f research objective; F2g/F2h data type. Within each pair, the first page shows research doctorates and the second master's works.
figures.alt: Eight portrait pages show the complete category vocabularies for study design, level of analysis, research objective and data type separately by degree. The left graph plots the observed percentage of eligible connected works in blue and remaining works in orange. Gray lines connect each group pair. The right graph plots the connected-minus-remaining percentage-point difference around a vertical zero line. Filled circles represent the full population and open circles the historical for-profit exclusion. All four group denominators appear above each graph. Small observed categories remain visible; all twelve overlapping data forms are retained. There are no interval bars. These are raw observed profiles, with field-composition checks supplied separately.

figures.title: Field composition
captions: **Caption.** Research-content contrasts before and after assigning a common field composition to works with and without an identified NIDA/NIAAA funding connection. Pages show research-doctorate and master's works separately. Each contrast is the connected-minus-remaining percentage-point difference for an outcome-specific usable-code population. Blue circles show the full crude contrast; open circles show the crude contrast restricted to fields having both connection groups; orange squares use the same pooled eligible field weights for both groups on that support. Connecting lines join alternative summaries and are not inferential intervals. The display retains the formerly highlighted eleven content categories and three doctoral research-objective examples, with master's counterparts; current main Figure 5C shows degree-field reach. Complete within-field category counts, group denominators, weights and profiles are in the numerical companions. Field-unavailable works remain a separate stratum. All twelve doctoral field strata are supported. Master's education has no connected works and is omitted from the common-support calculations, which retain approximately 99% of eligible works; full crude descriptions retain education. C8 data forms overlap. These observed and arithmetically reweighted descriptions do not establish a causal funding effect or adjust institution, period, or differences within broad fields. No inferential intervals are estimated.
figures.alt: **Alt text.** Two pages compare crude, common-support crude and common-field-mix contrasts for fourteen content categories per degree. Many research-doctorate contrasts shrink when field composition is equalized: nonrandomized experiments change from +33.4 to +13.6 points, molecular/cellular work from +9.3 to +0.4, nonhuman-organism work from +17.6 to +8.8, biological/physiological data from +26.2 to +9.2, and substance-action objectives from +7.9 to −0.1. Longitudinal observational work instead changes from +2.1 to +5.5 points. Master's nonrandomized-experiment and nonhuman-organism contrasts remain positive but smaller; small survey and service-objective contrasts change sign. Full crude and common-support crude values differ only for master's works because education lacks connected works. Every row supplies the three numerical contrasts; companion tables provide support and exact arithmetic.

figures.title: Opioid trends and completion windows
captions: **Supplementary Figure F4. Opioid-topic trends by identified NIDA connection and adjusted completion-window comparisons.** (A) Annual observed opioid shares for the full descriptive pair: 3,161 NIDA-connected works, including dual NIDA/NIAAA connections, and 9,160 works with no identified connection to either institute, across 2010–2023. The 906 NIAAA-only works are excluded. The dashed line marks the 2018 NIH HEAL launch as historical context. A work is counted once when its adopted S4 substance-label union contains an opioid label; known positives among incomplete labels are retained. (B) NIDA-by-post interactions from the two primary linear probability models, multiplied by 100, with pointwise institution-cluster CR1 95% confidence intervals and a t reference with G−1 degrees of freedom. The baseline is 2014–2017; post windows are 2021–2023 (beginning three years after the launch; 5,722 works, 421 institutions) and 2022–2023 (beginning four years after; 4,814 works, 395 institutions). Models include fixed effects for fine credential family, BF01–BF10 broad field, institution and completion year. These predictor-eligible samples differ from the full descriptive population in A. Positive values denote a larger adjusted absolute (percentage-point) increase among NIDA-connected works. Both intervals include zero; raw and two-test Holm p values appear in T10. The connection measure does not identify HEAL awards, and completion windows neither measure award-to-completion intervals nor isolate a causal funding effect; completions after 2023 are not observed. See S3 and the accompanying numerical appendix.
figures.note: The same figure appears as Figure S3.2 in the supplement.
figures.alt: **Alternative text.** Two-panel figure. Panel A shows annual opioid-topic percentages from 2010 to 2023 for NIDA-connected works, including dual connections, and works with no identified NIDA/NIAAA connection. Both groups rise over the period; in 2023 the shares are 33.3% and 19.6%, respectively. A dashed line marks the 2018 HEAL launch. Panel B shows adjusted absolute differential increases of 2.90 percentage points for the 2021–2023 window (95% CI −1.98 to 7.78) and 4.31 points for the 2022–2023 window (−1.36 to 9.97). Both intervals cross zero.

figures.title: Roles by degree, funding connection and destination
captions: Research and clinical-care roles by degree, identified funding connection and employment destination. Panel A has two labelled blocks. By degree shows five credential categories and ends with the bold All observations summary (n=307). By identified NIDA/NIAAA connection shows separate research-doctorate (PhD/ScD and equivalent; n=190) and pooled master's (general plus field-specific; 63 + 13 = 76) comparisons. Within research doctorates, 88 observations have an identified connection and 102 have no identified connection. Within pooled master's, the corresponding counts are 17 and 59. These four bars cover 266 observations. The group headers give full degree denominators and do not have bars. PsyD (n=24) and other named doctorate (n=17) observations remain in the degree block and the all-observation summary, but are not split by connection. Each bar uses its full printed observed denominator, including unscored observations. An identified connection means a in-scope NIDA/NIAAA-funded advisor or committee member, an individual-award association, or both under the adopted linkage and timing rules. No identified connection includes missing/unmatched roles and does not establish absence of support. Unscored counts are 0/1 for connected/no-identified-connection research doctorates and 1/2 for the corresponding master's groups. Panel B shows 120 of 190 research-doctorate and 57 of 76 pooled master's observations outside four-year colleges, universities and professional schools. Research doctorate (RD) is the upper bar and master's (M) the lower bar within each destination; numbers at right give destination counts. Segments use the full outside-degree denominator; destination rows sum to 100% for each degree. Two-year colleges and other education can remain included. Hospital jobs remain included despite academic affiliation. Unknown industry is excluded (one research-doctorate and three master's records).

Colors show the inclusive RC-RMI specification. Research only, Clinical care only and Both indicate which axes reach the likely-role threshold of 3; Other means neither does. Instrument U and unscored applicability are separate: Panel A has zero U and four unscored records; all Panel B records are scored. Printed percentages are rounded. The supplement pairs both specifications within each degree and supplies occupation composition and affiliation sensitivities.

Counts are unweighted linked observations, pending person reconciliation. Two approved later-PhD overrides preserve linked master's-thesis metadata; other records retain the linked-work degree basis. Industry is a scoring input.

figures.title: Roles by funding connection
captions: Research and clinical-care roles by identified NIDA/NIAAA funding connection, separately for research doctorates and master's degrees.

A: Research doctorates (PhD/ScD and equivalent; n=190), comparing 88 observations with an identified NIDA/NIAAA funding connection and 102 remaining observations. B: General and field-specific master's degrees pooled (n=76), comparing 17 connected and 59 remaining observations. Each stacked bar uses the full observed denominator printed beside that bar, including unscored records. PsyD (n=24) and other named doctorate (n=17) observations are outside this research-doctorate/master's comparison, leaving 266 of the 307 employment observations.

An identified connection is the adopted clear preceding-funded advisor/committee connection, clear individual-award association, or both, joined by scientific work key. Research-doctorate advisor/committee windows cover five preceding fiscal years; master's windows cover two, excluding completion fiscal year. Remaining observations have no identified connection under those rules, including missing or unmatched roles; this does not establish absence of support.

Colors and scores retain the existing inclusive RC-RMI specification and threshold of 3 on each role axis. Research only, Clinical care only and Both indicate which role axes reach that threshold; Other means neither does. Instrument U and unscored applicability are distinct. There are no U records. Unscored counts are 0/1 for connected/remaining research doctorates and 1/2 for connected/remaining master's observations. Counts are unweighted linked employment observations, pending person reconciliation. Printed percentages are rounded; exact values are in table `DEP4_funding_connection_roles`. These are descriptive observed comparisons, with no new models or inferential intervals.
